claims.text: The initial bulk MoNbTaW high-entropy alloy has a single-phase refractory BCC structure.
The BCC MoNbTaW alloy offers high structural stability.
Controlled oxygen incorporation into MoNbTaW forms a thin, uniform surface oxide/hydroxide layer enriched in Mo species.
The oxygen-induced Mo-oxide/hydroxide surface layer is stable.
Interstitial oxygen produces uniformly dispersed Mo-oxide/hydroxide clusters on the HEA surface.
The Mo-oxide/hydroxide surface species serve as active sites for hydrogen adsorption and reaction.
Interstitial oxygen alters the local electronic structure of Mo.
The oxygen-induced electronic modification of Mo facilitates adsorption and reaction of hydrogen intermediates.
The high-entropy MoNbTaW matrix provides excellent corrosion resistance under harsh electrochemical cycling.
The high-entropy MoNbTaW matrix provides mechanical durability under harsh electrochemical cycling.
Oxygen treatment enhances the HER catalytic activity of MoNbTaW relative to untreated MoNbTaW.
Oxygen treatment enhances the HOR catalytic activity of MoNbTaW relative to untreated MoNbTaW.
The oxygen-treated electrode will have lower HER and HOR onset overpotentials than the untreated electrode.
The oxygen-treated electrode will exhibit a more favorable Tafel slope than the untreated electrode.
The oxygen-treated electrode will deliver higher current density than the untreated electrode.
The oxygen-treated electrode will retain catalytic performance for longer electrochemical cycling than the untreated electrode.
Untreated MoNbTaW has inferior catalytic kinetics and durability because it lacks optimized active sites.
The catalytic benefit depends on achieving an optimal oxide-layer thickness.
An excessively thick or nonuniform oxide layer may impede electron transfer and reduce catalytic efficiency.
Acidic aqueous electrolyte such as 0.5 M H2SO4 at ambient to moderately elevated temperature is an intended operating condition for evaluating the material.
